resource_spec.name: elastic-ip
resource_spec.description: An elastic IP's real status in core vs. what CMP's cache says.

resource_spec.name: private-ip
resource_spec.description: A private IP/port's real status in core vs. what CMP's cache says.

update_elastic_ip.usage_note: The description field is CMP-only; allowed VIPs/CIDRs sync to core. Only the fields that sync to core can drift -- description changes never touch core at all.

update_private_ip.usage_note: The description field is CMP-only; allowed VIPs/CIDRs sync to core. Only the fields that sync to core can drift -- description changes never touch core at all.

create_floating_ip.usage_note: Returns in 'creating' status immediately -- the real allocation runs asynchronously through a FloatingIPCreatedEvent that settles the status once IaaS answers. Don't treat the initial response as final; the resource's real state isn't known until that event resolves.

delete_route_table.usage_note: Blocked for default or in-use route tables -- expect a validation error rather than a silent no-op if called on one of those.

accept_vpc_peering.usage_note: Accepts a pending VPC peering, which starts carrying real traffic between the two VPCs immediately. Confirm this is the intended peering before accepting -- reversing it means a separate delete_vpc_peering call.

attach_direct_connect_subnets.usage_note: Attaches private subnets to an existing Direct Connect, extending its reachable network range.

create_direct_connect.usage_note: Provisions a new Direct Connect (dedicated network link). A capacity/provisioning action, not typically reversible without a corresponding delete_direct_connect.

create_elastic_ip.usage_note: Allocates a new elastic IP from the region pool. Companion to create_floating_ip -- check which resource type the incident/customer actually needs before choosing between them.

create_route_table.usage_note: Creates a new route table and syncs it to core immediately -- unlike some network updates here, this one is not CMP-only.

create_rt_route.usage_note: Adds a route to a route table and pushes it to the core router immediately -- a routing change takes effect right away, not just in CMP's records.

create_vpc_peering.usage_note: Creates a VPC peering request between two zone-less, non-overlapping VPCs. Starts pending -- no traffic flows until accept_vpc_peering is called on it.

delete_direct_connect.usage_note: Removes a Direct Connect entirely. Breaks connectivity for anything relying on it -- confirm nothing is still using it first.

delete_elastic_ip.usage_note: Releases the elastic IP back to the region pool. Irreversible for this specific IP address -- a server relying on it loses that address permanently, not just temporarily.

delete_floating_ip.usage_note: Releases the floating IP back to the region pool. Same irreversibility as delete_elastic_ip -- confirm nothing is still using it.

delete_private_ip.usage_note: Deletes a private IP. Per the spec, blocked while still attached to a server -- expect a validation error rather than a silent detach-and-delete.

delete_rt_route.usage_note: Removes a route from a route table and from the core router immediately -- traffic relying on that route stops working right away.

delete_vpc_peering.usage_note: Deletes a VPC peering and every route-table route that used it as a nexthop. Broader blast radius than just the peering itself -- check list_rt_routes for routes depending on it first.

detach_direct_connect_subnets.usage_note: Detaches private subnets from a Direct Connect, narrowing its reachable network range. Anything in the detached subnets loses connectivity through this Direct Connect.

elastic_ip_update_port_security.usage_note: Toggles OpenStack port security (anti-spoofing + security-group enforcement) on this elastic IP's port. Setting port_security=false disables that protection -- a real security exposure, not a routine config change. Setting it back to true (the default) re-enables it.

get_floating_ip.usage_note: Check a floating IP's real status in core against what CMP's cache says -- same drift-checking role as get_elastic_ip for elastic IPs.

get_rt_route.usage_note: Detail for one route table route.

get_vpc_peering.usage_note: Detail and status for one VPC peering (pending/active/rejected).

list_rt_routes.usage_note: All route table routes -- check here before deleting a VPC peering or route table to see what still depends on it.

private_ip_update_port_security.usage_note: Toggles OpenStack port security (anti-spoofing + security-group enforcement) on this private IP's port. Setting port_security=false disables that protection -- a real security exposure, not a routine config change. Setting it back to true (the default) re-enables it.

reject_vpc_peering.usage_note: Rejects a pending VPC peering. Terminal per the spec -- it cannot be accepted after being rejected, a new create_vpc_peering would be needed instead.

update_direct_connect.usage_note: Updates a Direct Connect's own configuration.

update_floating_ip.usage_note: Updates the floating IP's description only -- DB-only, no core call, per the spec. Cannot drift from core since core is never involved.

update_route_table.usage_note: Core is only called when internet_access changes (per the spec) -- other field updates are CMP-only and can't drift from core.

update_vpc_peering.usage_note: Updates the VPC peering's description only -- CMP-only, no core call per the spec.
